The more important caveats are non-sampling: the LLM grader introduces its own error and version drift (see Known issues), and because SimpleQA reports three outcomes, a single 'accuracy' number hides whether a model is knowledgeable or merely bold — always read 'correct' alongside 'not attempted'.

metric.judge_model: Prompted ChatGPT classifier that compares the predicted answer to the reference (GPT-4o in OpenAI's reference implementation, simple-evals). Scores graded by different grader models or prompt versions are not strictly comparable.

contamination.mitigation: Public and ungated (openai/simple-evals), fully static, no refresh cycle. The irony is acute: a benchmark built to measure hallucination can itself be memorized. It was adversarially collected against 2024-era models, so the exact Q&A pairs — now discussed in papers, blog posts, and leaderboards — increasingly enter post-2024 training corpora, and a model can 'improve' by having seen the answer key rather than by knowing more. SimpleQA Verified (2025) partly re-collects and cleans to push back on this.

human_baseline.note: No human baseline — and arguably none is meaningful. The questions were deliberately selected to be obscure (adversarially filtered so frontier models got them wrong), so a human sitting the test closed-book would mostly measure luck, and open-book would measure Googling, not knowledge. The paper reports a 94.4% agreement rate from a third annotator, but that measures dataset quality (are the answers indisputable?), not human question-answering ability. This is the first benchmark on the wiki where a human reference line is not just missing but conceptually beside the point.

records.name: Soohak
records.short_description: Fresh research-level mathematics authored by mathematicians, plus unanswerable prompts that reward justified refusal.
records.status_evidence: The official July 2026 tracker reports 64.4% Avg@3 for the Challenge leader with 46 of 340 problems still unsolved by any tracked model; Refusal remains a separate hard target.
records.statistical_note: Challenge has 340 items and Refusal 99. Three samples reduce decoding noise but do not make Avg@3 a single-pass accuracy; judge error and subject mix remain material.

contamination.mitigation: Problems were newly authored without AI assistance under confidentiality controls; the full collection is embargoed until late 2026 and models are evaluated by request.

human_baseline.note: Five invited human teams collectively solved 50.6% of a 79-prompt sample, but this coverage result is not protocol-comparable to a single model's Avg@3.

records.name: StructFlowBench
records.short_description: 155 multi-turn dialogues scored on fine-grained constraints plus six inter-turn dialogue relationships (recall, refinement, expansion, follow-up, summary).
records.status_evidence: Moved to the site's nearing-saturation bucket: the best reported WCSR is already about 0.96 on a 155-dialogue public static set, while the remaining signal is concentrated in harder relationship slices such as refinement rather than the headline score.
records.statistical_note: 155 dialogues and a per-constraint score grid under a single LLM judge; per-turn and per-relationship cells are small. Treat WCSR gaps under a few points as noise until a leaderboard reports confidence intervals or a second judge.

metric.judge_model: GPT-4o (the paper's automated evaluator — see scoring methodology for the reproducibility caveat)

contamination.mitigation: The dataset was released on 2025-02-20 and postdates most 2024 training cutoffs, so direct memorization is currently less of a risk. The structural relationships are a behavioral/semantic target rather than a fixed factual test set, so memorizing one dialogue does little to help on unseen dialogue flows.

human_baseline.note: No protocol-comparable human baseline published. The 'Golden Context' setup drops each model into the same curated dialogue history rather than one it generated, but the paper reports no human agreement with the GPT-4o judge on model outputs.

records.name: SuperGLUE
records.short_description: Eight English NLU tasks spanning question answering, inference, causal reasoning, word sense, and coreference.
records.status_evidence: The official aggregate human estimate (89.8) was crossed by a single DeBERTa model (89.9) by 2020-12-29; the 2022 leaderboard leader reached 91.3, leaving a narrow, noisy ceiling.
records.statistical_note: The aggregate is not a sample-size-weighted accuracy and has no single binomial confidence interval. CB, COPA, and WSC have especially small evaluation splits, while metric and prompt implementation differences can exceed small leaderboard gaps.

contamination.mitigation: Official test labels were kept private behind the evaluation server, but test inputs, training and development data, source corpora, and benchmark examples are static and public. Modern harnesses normally score the labeled public validation splits, so those runs have no held-out-label protection.

human_baseline.note: Official aggregate estimate. Per-task estimates mix prior published results with crowdworker reannotation; paired metrics are averaged before the eight-task macro-average.

records.name: SWE-bench
records.short_description: Real GitHub issues from 12 Python repositories, solved by generating patches that must pass repository tests.
records.status_evidence: SWE-bench Verified superseded the original test set in 2024 after human review found underspecified tasks and tests that rejected valid fixes.
records.statistical_note: At 2,294 items, a 50% resolve rate has an approximate 95% binomial interval of ±2.0 points; task and repository clustering makes a simple binomial interval optimistic.

contamination.mitigation: Evaluation starts from a historical base commit, but issues, merged pull requests, gold patches, and tests are public in repository history.

human_baseline.note: No protocol-comparable aggregate human score was published. Every instance has a human-authored pull request, but that does not establish a timed blind-test pass rate.

records.name: SWE-bench Pro
records.short_description: Long-horizon repository tasks across public, held-out, and commercial codebases, with a continuing public model leaderboard.
records.status_evidence: The benchmark still has a maintained public leaderboard and substantial score spread: the 2026-08-03 LLM Stats snapshot ranges from 0.584 to 0.800 across these 17 leading models, despite documented task-quality concerns.
records.statistical_note: At 731 items and 50% resolution, the nominal 95% binomial interval is about ±3.6 points. The 2026 audit's estimated ~30% broken-task rate dominates that sampling uncertainty. Dates on the 17 newest timeline points denote the 2026-08-03 LLM Stats snapshot, not individual evaluation or model-launch dates.

metric.primary: resolved instances on the public set (%)

contamination.mitigation: Public and held-out OSS repositories use strong-copyleft licenses as a legal deterrent to training inclusion; the commercial split uses private proprietary code. Neither is a technical guarantee.

human_baseline.note: No protocol-comparable aggregate human score is published. The authors describe tasks as requiring hours to days for professionals, and tasks have human reference solutions.

records.name: SWE-bench Verified
records.short_description: A 500-task, engineer-reviewed subset of SWE-bench that became the standard repository-level coding-agent test.
records.status_evidence: Classified saturated on 2026-02-17: under the standardized mini-SWE-agent 2.0.0 protocol, the leading results clustered at 76.8%, 75.8%, 75.8%, and 75.6%, limiting discrimination among frontier systems; separate contamination and task-quality concerns remain documented below.
records.statistical_note: At 500 items, a 50% resolve rate has an approximate 95% binomial interval of ±4.4 points; repository clustering, flaky environments, and test defects add non-sampling uncertainty.

contamination.mitigation: Three professional developers screened each candidate for issue and test quality, but the issues, gold patches, and repository histories remain public and static.

human_baseline.note: No protocol-comparable aggregate human pass rate was published. Annotators estimated fix time, and each task has a human-authored pull request, but neither is a blind human baseline.

records.name: SWE-Lancer
records.short_description: Current 198-task offline patch benchmark derived from paid Upwork work, with historical mixed implementation and manager-task variants.
records.status_evidence: The maintained leaderboard is frozen at July 2025 and narrows paper-era Diamond from 502 mixed tasks to 198 offline IC tasks, making unlabeled Diamond claims non-comparable.
records.statistical_note: The current offline leaderboard has 198 executable patch tasks. The original paper's 502-task Diamond mixed 237 IC and 265 manager tasks, so its overall accuracy is a different axis.

metric.primary: pass@1 accuracy on the 198-task Diamond offline subset (%)

contamination.mitigation: The benchmark uses a fixed historical codebase and, since July 2025, removes live Internet dependencies from execution; the public Diamond tasks and code are nevertheless exposed.

human_baseline.note: No blind protocol-comparable aggregate human baseline is reported. Original freelancers completed the IC work and hired managers chose proposals, defining the references rather than a timed test score.

records.name: TabMWP
records.short_description: Grade-level math word problems that require combining a question with structured, textual, or image-rendered tables.
records.status_evidence: The official leaderboard reports Chameleon with GPT-4 at 98.78% on text-ground-truth tables, above the published 90.22% human estimate; the fixed public test set no longer separates frontier tool systems.
records.statistical_note: The test split is large, but errors are clustered by source table and answer format; close results must use the same table representation, prompt selection, tools, and parsing rules.

contamination.mitigation: None beyond fixed train/dev/test splits; all tables, solutions, and test answers are public in the repository.

human_baseline.note: Official test-set estimate reported by the benchmark authors; subgroup accuracy varies by free-text, multiple-choice, and answer type.

records.name: Terminal-Bench
records.short_description: Eighty-nine realistic terminal tasks graded in containers; version 2.1 repairs 2.0's dependency, resource, and specification defects.
records.status_evidence: Terminal-Bench 2.1 remains actively maintained and submission-driven; its verified 17-entry leaderboard spans 58.7% to 83.8% across multiple agent-model pairs, while Terminal-Bench 3.0 is still in development.
records.statistical_note: With only 89 tasks, one task changes accuracy by about 1.12 points and a 50% pass rate has a nominal 95% interval near ±10.4 points. Agent/model pair, trial count, resources, and task version are essential.

contamination.mitigation: Task repositories include a canary asking training pipelines to exclude benchmark data; 2.1 adds continuous dependency and oracle validation, but neither prevents public-task memorization.

human_baseline.note: No aggregate blind human baseline is published. Every 2.0 task has a human-written solution and expert-time metadata, establishing solvability but not a comparable score.

records.name: Tool Decathlon / Toolathlon
records.short_description: A long-horizon tool-use benchmark with 108 tasks across 32 software applications, 604 MCP tools, and state-based evaluators.
records.status_evidence: Toolathlon-Verified is the current benchmark release as of 2026-06-30. The official site reports 108 tasks, 32 MCP servers with 604 tools, 7 local toolkits, and a current Verified leaderboard.
records.statistical_note: Toolathlon-Verified starts a new official score series. Do not compare Verified results directly with the archived pre-Verified leaderboard.

contamination.mitigation: Toolathlon-Verified reviewed prompts, ground truths, evaluators, initial states, and infrastructure; state-based scripts improve grading reliability but do not hide public tasks.

human_baseline.note: No single protocol-comparable human baseline is published for the full Toolathlon-Verified set.

records.name: TruthfulQA
records.short_description: 817 adversarial questions probing whether models repeat common human misconceptions — famous for finding that bigger models were often less truthful.
records.status_evidence: By 2023 post-RLHF models exceeded the 94% human truthfulness baseline — but largely because the exact misconceptions TruthfulQA targets are what alignment tuning trains against, and the dataset itself leaked into alignment mixes. Saturation here reflects targeted contamination, not broadly truthful models. saturated_date (2023-06) marks the ChatGPT/GPT-4 era when the inverse-scaling trend reversed.
records.statistical_note: 817 questions → roughly ±3pt across the 60–90% range (95% CI). The 38 category splits (some <20 questions) are far too small for per-category comparison. Metric choice (MC1 vs MC2 vs generation) moves scores more than most model-to-model gaps do.

metric.primary: MC2 (normalized probability mass on true answers, %)

contamination.mitigation: None, and uniquely self-defeating: the misconceptions TruthfulQA targets are exactly what RLHF and Constitutional-style alignment tuning is trained to avoid, and the dataset itself appears in some alignment/instruction mixes. Modern scores partly measure exposure to the benchmark's own patterns.

human_baseline.note: 94% truthful on the generation task in the original paper (human validators). No published human baseline exists for the MC1/MC2 multiple-choice variants, so the timeline and gauge track generation truthfulness to stay comparable to this number.

records.name: Video-MME
records.short_description: Video-understanding benchmark with 900 videos, 2,700 questions, three duration bands, subtitles, and audio.
records.status_evidence: The maintainers launched Video-MME-v2 in 2026 because existing video benchmarks were saturating and did not match user experience; new evaluations should prefer v2's grouped temporal-reasoning protocol.
records.statistical_note: Frame sampling can move scores materially. Comparisons must match the number/resolution of frames and the subtitle/audio condition; duration-band averages should accompany the overall score.

contamination.mitigation: Questions were newly human-authored and filtered against text-only answering, but the videos are public YouTube material and the complete annotations are now public.

human_baseline.note: No single protocol-comparable human aggregate for the original Video-MME is recorded here.

records.name: WinoGrande
records.short_description: Binary fill-in-the-blank commonsense problems, scaled from Winograd schemas and adversarially filtered to reduce dataset shortcuts.
records.status_evidence: The original XL result was 79.1% against a 94.0% human estimate, leaving real headroom, but the static public inputs and widespread validation-set use make modern scores contamination-sensitive.
records.statistical_note: On the 1,267-example validation split, a 50% accuracy estimate has an approximate 95% binomial margin of error of +/-2.8 points; paired predictions are preferable for close model comparisons.

contamination.mitigation: Official test labels remain hidden, and lm-evaluation-harness exposes a decontamination query, but the test inputs and the fully labeled validation split are public and unchanged.

human_baseline.note: Crowd-worker estimate reported by the original paper; compare with care because current lm-eval runs use the validation split rather than the hidden-label official test set.

records.name: ZeroSCROLLS
records.short_description: Zero-shot long-text suite derived from SCROLLS with test-only tasks and new aggregation-style long-context challenges.
records.status_evidence: ZeroSCROLLS fixed SCROLLS' fine-tuning mismatch and has a live leaderboard, but its 2023-era tasks are now shorter and narrower than current 100k+ and multi-needle long-context stress suites.
records.statistical_note: The validation sets are tiny and meant for eyeballing; use held-out leaderboard evaluation for claims. The visual graph on this page deliberately plots only the official ZeroSCROLLS paper Table 3 Avg column from the leaderboard at the time of writing. It does not plot per-task scores or later leaderboard submissions.

contamination.mitigation: ZeroSCROLLS removes training data and uses small validation sets, but the task definitions and component sources are public.

human_baseline.note: No single suite-wide human baseline is recorded here; component tasks have their own annotation histories.
